Reads the AAPS log and looks at what AutoISF did. The suggestions are careful, but they are only a help: you decide. Change one setting at a time and watch it for a few days.

string.name: autoisf_log_days
string.comment: Button to choose the period. %1$d=number of days. Example: 3 d

resources.string: No AutoISF loop runs found in the log for this period.
The log could not be read: %1$s

string.name: autoisf_log_period_value
string.comment: %1$s=start date and time, %2$s=end date and time

string.name: autoisf_log_runs_value
string.comment: %1$d=number of loop runs, %2$s=hours, already formatted with unit. Example: 576 (48.00 h), 21 files

string.name: autoisf_log_smbs_value
string.comment: %1$d=number of SMBs, %2$s=insulin, already formatted. Example: 42 (12.35 U)

resources.string: Runs with SMB from even target

string.name: autoisf_log_lows_value
string.comment: %1$d=number of lows, %2$d=how many of them came after an SMB. Example: 3 (2 after SMB)

resources.string: SMB stopped for a predicted low after an SMB

string.name: autoisf_log_not_enough_data
string.comment: %1$s=hours analyzed, %2$s=hours needed, both already formatted with unit. Example: 0.42 h, 12.00 h

resources.string: Only %1$s of loop runs with the same settings. Suggestions need at least %2$s. Choose a longer period or wait.
AutoISF settings were changed at %1$s. Only the time after this change is used.

string.name: autoisf_log_event_low
string.comment: %1$s=time of the SMB, %2$s=SMB in U, %3$s=BG at the SMB with unit, %4$s=ISF factor, %5$s=which factor drove it, %6$s=lowest BG with unit, %7$s=time of the low. Example: 14:09 SMB 0.95 U at 9.7 mmol/l, ISF ×1.31 (bg_ISF) → low 3.6 mmol/l at 16:20

resources.string: %1$s SMB %2$s U at %3$s, ISF ×%4$s (%5$s) → low %6$s at %7$s

string.name: autoisf_log_event_predicted
string.comment: Same as autoisf_log_event_low, but BG did not go low: the loop predicted a low and stopped SMB. %6$s=BG at that time with unit, %7$s=time
